svg.title: Emission spectra of light sources
svg.desc: Relative intensity versus wavelength from 400 to 700 nm. Curve A, average sunlight at Earth’s surface, is fairly flat, between about 80 and 125. Curve B, a fluorescent lamp, is a broad hump with sharp spikes near 405, 436, 546 and 578 nm. Curve C, an incandescent bulb, rises steadily from about 15 at 400 nm to about 190 at 700 nm. Curve D, a helium-neon laser, is a single narrow spike at 633 nm reaching about 210.
